findings.title: signal: SignalConfig is dead-end plumbing in execute_optimization and _build_cv_callable
findings.summary: execute_optimization declares signal: SignalConfig (line 90), forwards it to _build_cv_callable (line 103), and _build_cv_callable accepts it as a required keyword argument (line 247). Inside _build_cv_callable the local variable signal is never referenced; _evaluate_cv_slice does not accept it; no downstream consumer reads any attribute of it. Verified via grep across the runner module that nothing past the parameter binding uses signal.<X> in any branch.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'signal' research/aegis_research/optimization/runner.py shows three lines: 90 (parameter), 103 (forwarded), 247 (parameter). No reads. Callers in research/aegis_research/strategy_runs.py:230 and 30+ test sites construct SignalConfig() purely to satisfy the keyword.
findings.rationale: Per Forward-First and KISS in AGENTS.md the substrate migration removed signal-era execution; the empty SignalConfig() forced on every caller is exactly the kind of dead plumbing the deletion targets enumerated. The reader has to wade through SignalConfig imports and constructions across 30+ tests with no payoff. The plan U7 deviation notes the parameter was retained, but retention is unjustified once the signal path is gone.
findings.suggested_action: Drop the signal parameter from execute_optimization and _build_cv_callable; update strategy_runs.py and every test_optimization_*.py call site to stop passing it; remove the SignalConfig import in runner.py. If SignalConfig still has value at the configuration boundary for market_data loading, it stays — but should not transit the optimization runner.
findings.anchor_match: 75 (objectively provable: the parameter is taken and never read in the module)

findings.title: open_prices/open_slice plumbing is unused — branch is dead indirection
findings.summary: execute_optimization accepts open_prices: pd.DataFrame | None (line 86), threads has_open_prices into _build_cv_callable (line 107), and passes (close, open_prices) tuple to the decorated cv_split callable (line 126). _build_cv_callable then branches on has_open_prices producing two near-identical closures (lines 263-291). The has_open_prices=True closure has signature (close_slice, open_slice, **params) but its body passes only close_slice forward to _evaluate_cv_slice; open_slice is silently dropped. No code reads open prices anywhere downstream — the new PFO.from_filled_allocations + from_optimizer substrate is close-only.
findings.evidence: Line 265 defines cv_callable(close_slice, open_slice, **params) but the call on lines 266-275 forwards only close_slice. _evaluate_cv_slice (line 294) has no open_slice/open_prices parameter. Same for cv_callable_no_open. preflight.py:71 still computes materialized_frame_count = 4 + int(has_open_prices) suggesting plumbing is half-cleaned.
findings.rationale: Two branches that do the same thing, both ending in a function call that ignores the difference — this is unnecessary indirection (two layers of branching with zero observable behavior difference) compounded with dead code (the open_slice argument). A reader spending time understanding why VBT receives an open_prices takeable_arg has nothing to learn at the end.
findings.suggested_action: Drop open_prices from execute_optimization signature, drop the has_open_prices branch from _build_cv_callable so only the close-only closure remains, drop call_args = (close, open_prices) tuple at line 126, and remove the has_open_prices plumbing from preflight.py if it has no other consumer.
findings.anchor_match: 75 (objectively provable: open_slice closure parameter is bound and discarded)

findings.title: _next_open_executable_mask name describes deleted next-open execution timing
findings.summary: The helper _next_open_executable_mask retains naming from the signal-era 'next_open' execution timing. The new contract is close-decision close-execution (diagnostics emit 'execution_timing': 'close' at portfolios.py:238). The function actually computes a contiguous-rows mask — rows that are not preceded by a market-index gap. The name advertises a concept the substrate no longer has.
findings.evidence: portfolios.py:238 declares execution_timing='close'. The function body computes contiguous = positions[1:] == positions[:-1] + 1; it has nothing to do with next-open execution.
findings.rationale: The next developer reading apply_executable_mask_and_terminal_liquidation will mis-model the semantics. The name describes a how/legacy concept ('next_open') rather than what it computes ('contiguous bars', 'no gap').
findings.suggested_action: Rename to _contiguous_rows_executable_mask or _no_gap_executable_mask. Pure rename, no behavior change. Update the call site at masking.py:19.
findings.anchor_match: 50 (naming judgment, but anchored: the literal token 'next_open' refers to a substrate the PR deleted)

findings.title: simulate_portfolio and simulate_portfolio_batch are 85% duplicated
findings.summary: Both functions call apply_executable_mask_and_terminal_liquidation, then vbt.PFO.from_filled_allocations with identical kwargs (valid_only=True, nonzero_only=False, unique_only=False), then vbt.Portfolio.from_optimizer with kwargs that differ only by close frame, group_by, and the post-hoc diagnostic decoration. The batch flavor additionally calls _validate_candidate_columns + expand_market_frame_to_candidate_columns up front and patches diagnostics['shape'] and overrides diagnostics['grouping'] after the shared _portfolio_diagnostics build.
findings.evidence: Lines 60-65 vs 109-114 (identical PFO call). Lines 66-78 vs 115-127 (Portfolio.from_optimizer differs only in close, group_by). Lines 142-148 in batch re-assigns diagnostics['grouping'] that _portfolio_diagnostics just computed.
findings.rationale: The grouping dict being computed inside _portfolio_diagnostics and then overwritten in simulate_portfolio_batch is a clear sign the shared helper signature is wrong — the caller knows the truth and discards the helper's guess. Extract a private _simulate_with_grouping(close, masked, config, *, group_by, group_label, candidate_ids) that callers parameterize. simulate_portfolio_batch keeps its column-validation + close-expansion prelude.
findings.suggested_action: Introduce a private helper that does PFO build + Portfolio.from_optimizer + diagnostic assembly parameterized by group_by/label/candidate_ids; have both public functions call into it. Eliminates the diagnostics['grouping'] double-assign.
findings.anchor_match: 50 (judgment about extraction threshold; clear DRY surface but reasonable people could leave it)

findings.title: _convert_active applies redundant decided mask after coercing NaN to False
findings.summary: _convert_active builds decided = frame.notna() and selected = _coerce_active_to_bool(frame) (which uses np.where(pd.isna, False, value) — every NaN cell becomes False). Line 97 then does selected = selected & decided, but selected is already False wherever decided is False, so the AND is a no-op. The defensive belt-and-braces obscures the actual contract: 'NaN means undecided which means not selected'.
findings.evidence: _coerce_active_to_bool (lines 121-124) returns False at every NaN. AND-ing with notna() cannot turn True into False except where coerce already produced False.
findings.rationale: Minor noise. Reader has to verify the redundancy isn't compensating for a subtle case. Removing makes intent clear.
findings.suggested_action: Drop line 97 (selected = selected & decided). Add a unit-test comment that NaN-active is treated as False.

residual_risks.title: policy.target_exposure_cap > 0 check duplicates schema validation
residual_risks.summary: policy.convert_to_allocations rejects target_exposure_cap <= 0, but configuration/validation.py:855 already enforces positive=True at the config boundary. Either the duplicated check is defensive (acceptable as a substrate-boundary guard) or it indicates distrust of the schema. Documenting which intent applies would help; not blocking.

residual_risks.title: Three frozen module-level VBT constants (VBT_PORTFOLIO_FACTORY, VBT_PF_METHOD, VBT_RESOLVED_SIZE_TYPE) are used exactly once in simulate_portfolio + once in simulate_portfolio_batch + once in _portfolio_diagnostics
residual_risks.summary: Borderline premature naming. They make the diagnostics block self-documenting and link the call-site value to the diagnostic value. Keeping them is defensible. Flagging only because if the DRY refactor in maint-4 lands, the redundancy goes away naturally.

testing_gaps.title: No test asserts that the optimization runner does not depend on signal parameter contents
testing_gaps.summary: Every test passes signal=SignalConfig() (default). If the parameter is retained for any reason after addressing maint-1, a test that varies signal values and asserts identical results would document that retention. Conversely, removing the parameter (recommended) makes this gap moot.
